tasks.title: The snapshot says what's allowed and what to watch
tasks.summary: Registry rows carry the status writes ws act would accept, and the snapshot lists every path whose change alters a view, which ws serve also uses.
acceptance: a test shows an active row's actions are ["pause"], a paused row's ["resume"], a done row's [], and a progress-stale row's include "sync"
a test shows act refuses exactly what a row's actions leave out, read from the one table in snapshot.py
a test shows refresh holds the registry, each workstream folder recursively, and git's HEAD, index, packed-refs, refs/heads and worktrees
test_serve shows the server's watched paths are expanded from refresh, and an evidence file still reaches an open event stream
the snapshot with both fields passes its schema, and make test passes

tasks.title: ws review --show gives one side of a diff
tasks.summary: One file's content on the old or new side of a task's review range, with a branch review's old side at the merge base.
acceptance: a test with main moved after a task's claim shows --side old of a branch review is the merge base's content, not main's tip
tests cover an added file (old text null), a deleted file (new text null), a modified file and a binary file (binary true, no text)
a path not in the task's diffstat is refused with a non-zero exit, as --file is
a test in tests/test_review.py shows the output passes schema/review-show.schema.json, plain ws review is unchanged, and make test passes

tasks.title: The extension's package, CLI module and test harness
tasks.summary: ui/vscode builds with tsc, activates in VS Code, finds the project through ws root, and has unit, source and integration tests wired into make.
acceptance: make test-vscode builds with tsc and runs an integration test in the installed VS Code, with no download, in which the extension activates on a sample project and loads its snapshot
the integration test runs the branch's CLI through workstreams.wsCommand, not the ws on the PATH
a folder that isn't a project and a missing ws each show their message, and nothing else runs
tests/test_vscode_files.py runs the node logic tests, finds no project or agent literal in ui/vscode/src, and shows the real CLI accepts each argv cli.ts builds
make vsix produces a .vsix, and package.json declares untrusted and virtual workspaces unsupported
.workstream/config.toml has a [worktree] setup line installing ui/vscode's locked dependencies
tasks.notes: The first npm install needs the network; the lockfile is committed.

tasks.title: Registry, tasks, documents, status bar and live refresh
tasks.summary: The Registry tree, task tooltips, documents in Markdown preview and the status bar, kept current by watchers on the snapshot's refresh paths.
acceptance: logic tests cover waveLine, badgesOf, lanes and splitRows with the cases ui/web/tests/logic.test.mjs uses
an integration test shows the Registry tree's workstreams, phases and tasks, in priority order with their badges, on a sample project
an integration test shows a claim made from a shell reaches the tree without a manual refresh
a source test shows every MarkdownString built from repo text uses appendText, with isTrusted and supportHtml off
Show done adds closed workstreams, and each document opens in Markdown preview

tasks.title: Writes through ws act, and launching in a terminal
tasks.summary: Pause, resume, sync and unclaim behind a modal with pinned revisions; Run, Coordinate, Close and Abandon start the configured agent in a terminal, or copy the prompt.
acceptance: an integration test shows a confirmed pause on a sample project commits through ws act and the tree shows paused
an integration test commits from a shell while the modal is open; confirming shows act's stale-view refusal, and HEAD and the tree are unchanged
commands appear only where the snapshot's row actions or a finding's actions offer them
an integration test shows Run with workstreams.agentCommand set creates a terminal whose shellPath and shellArgs carry the prompt as one argument, with cwd at the root
with no agent command, Run copies the prompt; Abandon asks for a reason first
launch targets live in one module that a chat target could join without changing the callers

tasks.title: The review queue and diffs in the diff editor
tasks.summary: The review queue, each task's gates and acceptance-with-proof, its evidence in the editor, and its files in the built-in diff editor through ws review --show.
acceptance: logic tests cover gateSummary and rangeLine with the web UI's cases
an integration test shows the queue lists branch work before landed work
an integration test opens a branch task's file after main moved, and the diff editor's two sides match ws review --show old and new
a binary file opens no diff and says so, and an added file's old side is empty
each acceptance item shows its proof or that it has none, and the evidence file opens in the editor

tasks.title: Health in the Problems panel, and the budget
tasks.summary: Health findings as a tree and as diagnostics with quick fixes through the same confirm, and the context budget from ws audit context --json.
acceptance: an integration test with a stale claim shows its finding in the Health tree and as a diagnostic on that workstream's tasks file
the finding's quick fix opens the same confirm, and confirming unclaims through ws act
diagnostics clear when the finding goes
the Budget view shows each role's used and limit from ws audit context --json, and runs it only when visible

tasks.title: Prove it in VS Code, and write down what's true
tasks.summary: The packaged .vsix installed in the real VS Code, every view and write checked by hand on a sample project and read-only on this repo, then the guide, the decision record and the plan's status.
acceptance: evidence records make vsix and code --install-extension installing it into VS Code 1.139

evidence records, on a sample project built from an installed wheel: every view drawn, a pause landing, a stale pause refused with HEAD unchanged, a branch diff after main moved, a quick-fix unclaim, and Run in a terminal
evidence records this repo viewed with HEAD, status and refs unchanged afterwards

acceptance.text: The owner sees the extension drawn in VS Code

acceptance: docs/decisions/0017-vscode-extension.md has what was shown and what is not proven, and docs/plan.md's status row for M9 links it

inScope: the VS Code extension in ui/vscode
additive snapshot facts: row actions and refresh paths
outOfScope: chat windows as a launch target
moving the web UI or the pane onto the new facts
